svg.title: Step-up human verification for agent-driven browsers: AWS WAF Bot Control, Amazon CloudFront, Lambda@Edge, and Amazon Rekognition Face Liveness
svg.text: Step-up human verification for agent-driven browsers
AWS WAF Bot Control decides when · Lambda@Edge decides how · Amazon Rekognition Face Liveness checks for a live person
CHECK FOR A LIVE PERSON · FLAGGED SESSIONS ONLY
Each is bound to the AWS WAF token ID that minted it. Secure + HttpOnly.
proves the browser was flagged; carries return path
binds the Face Liveness session ID to this browser
a live person passed; works only with the same WAF token
Direct from the browser / on failure
Step in the request flow (see README)
AWS WAF evaluates each request when CloudFront receives it, before the cache and before any Lambda@Edge function runs.
Lambda@Edge functions are created in us-east-1, run at CloudFront Regional Edge Caches, and call the us-east-1 services shown.
Also in the stack: IAM roles and policies, response headers policies, origin access controls, and CDK-managed custom resources. Icons: AWS Architecture Icons.
